name: local_export
description:
Export from the editor's currently-open project to a local file on this desktop machine. This tool directly handles finished video, audio, transparent Motion Graphic media, subtitle files, NLE XML for Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve, and editable 剪映专业版 / CapCut drafts; do not load an export skill or direct the user to the Export dialog. Exporting to 剪映专业版 or CapCut is its own capability here — format="jianying" hands them the timeline as a draft they open and keep editing.

Video and audio plus Motion Graphic ProRes renders run in the desktop app's native flux engine. Local video export supports 480p, 720p, 1080p, and 4K plus 24, 25, 30, 50, and 60 fps; omit either setting to use the editor's current export setting. Local source files stay on this machine, and cloud-only assets are mirrored into the desktop media directory before export. Subtitle and XML artifacts use the open editor's active timeline/caption state and are saved to the requested local path. Motion Graphic export requires ChatCut Pro. Omit motionGraphicItemId when the active timeline has exactly one Motion Graphic; when it has several, the tool returns their item IDs, asset IDs, and start frames so you can retry without another project read.

format="jianying" writes an editable draft into 剪映专业版 / CapCut's own project directory — not to a path you choose, so outputPath is rejected — and copies the timeline's media in beside it. The draft name comes from the project and is made unique, so an export never overwrites a draft the user already has. The user gets a dialog offering to open the app; do not tell them to go looking for the folder, and do not try to launch the app yourself.

Returns { outputPath, taskId }. Native renders return once queued and continue in the background, with progress visible in Export History. Subtitle, XML, and 剪映 draft artifacts are already written when this tool returns; for a draft, outputPath is the draft folder. The editor must have this session's target project open; if a different project is open, this tool errors out and the user needs to switch projects first.

codec.description: Codec for video/audio only. format="video" supports "h264" (default). format="audio" supports "mp3" (default) or "wav".

format.description: Export kind: "video" (default), "audio", "motion_graphic" (transparent ProRes 4444 .mov), "subtitles", "xml", or "jianying" (an editable 剪映专业版 / CapCut draft).

fps.description: Video output frame rate for format="video". Supported values are 24, 25, 30, 50, and 60. Omit to use the editor's current export frame-rate setting.

includeMotionGraphics.description: For format="jianying". Motion graphics are rendered into the draft as transparent video clips, which requires ChatCut Pro; pass false to export the draft without them. Defaults to true.

motionGraphicItemId.description: Optional for format="motion_graphic". Timeline item id or unambiguous id prefix for the Motion Graphic instance to export exactly as previewed, including property overrides. Omit it to auto-select the only Motion Graphic on the active timeline or receive actionable candidates when several exist.

nleFormat.description: XML target for format="xml": "fcp_xml" for Premiere Pro (default) or "fcp_xml_resolve" for DaVinci Resolve. Not the route to 剪映 or CapCut — those take format="jianying".

outputPath.description: Optional destination path. Extensions are .mp4 for video, .mp3/.wav for audio, .mov for Motion Graphics, .srt/.txt for subtitles, and .xml for XML. Relative paths are saved under the OS Videos directory in a ChatCut/ subfolder. During an agent turn, an absolute path outside that folder opens the native Save dialog and requires the user to approve the destination.

product.description: Target app for format="jianying": "jianying" (剪映专业版) or "capcut". Omit when only one is installed; when both are, the tool returns an error naming them so you can retry with the one the user wants.

resolution.description: Video resolution for format="video": "480p", "720p", "1080p", or "4K". Omit to use the editor's current export resolution setting. Unlike cloud export, local export supports 4K.

subtitleFormat.description: Subtitle file type for format="subtitles": "srt" (default) or "txt".
